title: machine: ensure OCI pull cache directory exists
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes `podman machine init` failing on Windows with:

```text
The system cannot find the path specified.
```

when the OCI machine image cache parent directory does not exist.

## Why?

`pkg/machine/ocipull/pull.go` passes the destination path to `layout.ParseReference()`. On Windows, the path resolution performed by `containers/image` requires the parent directory to exist.

When the cache parent directory is missing, this results in `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`.

This change creates the destination's parent directory with `os.MkdirAll()` before calling `layout.ParseReference()`.

The final OCI layout directory is not created beforehand. It is still created by `containers/image` during the pull.

## Testing

Added a regression test covering the missing parent directory case.

The following targeted test passes:

```text
go test -tags containers_image_openpgp ./pkg/machine/ocipull -run TestPullCreatesParentDirectory -v
```

The complete `pkg/machine/ocipull` package test suite also passes.

Fixes #29639

@Luap99 I investigated this further based on your questions.

`GetMachineDirs()` normally creates the image cache directory with `os.MkdirAll()`. When that directory is missing, `layout.ParseReference()` fails in `ResolvePathToFullyExplicit()` because the parent directory must already exist. The `ensureDirectoryExists()` call in `containers/image` happens later, after `ParseReference()` succeeds, so it cannot handle this particular failure.

I also confirmed that this path resolution requirement is not Windows-specific. The Windows-specific part is the error returned when the parent path is missing.

My `MkdirAll()` addition before `ParseReference()` therefore fixes the immediate failure, but I still cannot explain why the cache directory was missing in the first place, given that `GetMachineDirs()` normally creates it. So I don't think I have enough evidence to say that my PR addresses the actual root cause.

I'd prefer to close #29662 rather than submit a workaround without understanding the underlying issue.

Thanks for pointing this out. I also understand the concerns regarding the project's contribution and LLM guidelines, and I'll make sure to follow them strictly going forward.
